reserve.who: The renter, on their own phone
reserve.body: Priya books an e-bike for three days. She pays the rental fee, reads the damage price list and approves a hold in PayPal. The money is reserved in her own account, and nothing is charged.

points.a: The rental fee is paid. The deposit is only held. The page says which is which in one sentence.
points.b: The damage prices are shown and agreed before anything is approved.

handOver.body: Jonas opens the rental on his phone and is led through six views of the bike. It takes about forty seconds. Priya gets the condition report on her phone and confirms it.

points.a: An outline shows how to frame each view, one after another.
points.b: A blurred or dark photograph is caught at once and taken again.
points.c: Marks already on the item are recorded, so nobody is charged for them later.

return.body: Jonas takes the same six photographs. Hold lines each one up with its twin from the handover and outlines what changed. Drag between the two photographs to see it.

points.a: The return repeats the handover shot for shot.
points.b: Each difference gets one of three answers: no change, ordinary wear or damage.
points.c: When the photographs do not allow a confident answer, Hold says so and a person looks at the item.

settle.body: A clean return ends at the counter. Damage becomes an itemized claim that a person approves, and the renter sees it before anything is taken.

points.a: Nothing new: one confirmation releases the whole hold and tells the renter.
points.b: Damage: staff or the owner can accept, reduce, remove or add items before anything is charged.
points.c: Only the approved amount is taken. The rest is released at once.

ai.title: The AI compares. A person decides.
ai.lead: Automated damage charging made rental customers angry because nobody could be asked. Hold is built the other way round: the AI gathers and compares, a person decides, and the renter sees everything.
ai.listsHeading: What the AI does, and what it never does

limits.title: Honest about its limits.
limits.lead: Lighting, dirt and reflections can mislead any comparison.

confidence.title: It states its confidence
confidence.body: Each finding says how sure the comparison is, in words a renter can read.

retake.title: It asks for a retake
retake.body: A blurred or dark photograph is caught on the phone, while it is still easy to take again.

defers.title: It defers to a person
defers.body: When it cannot tell wear from damage, it says so and a person looks. The manual path always works.

pipeline.title: Seven steps. The model gets one.
pipeline.lead: The cheapest reliable method goes first. Anything that must not be missed is found by plain code, and still works when the model is down.

quality.title: Check the photograph
quality.body: On the phone, as it is taken. A blurred, dark or badly framed shot is rejected at once.

normalize.title: Even it out
normalize.body: Orientation, size and exposure are corrected.

align.title: Line it up
align.body: The return photograph is aligned with its twin from the handover.

regions.title: Find what changed
regions.body: Areas that differ are marked as hints for the next step.

judge.title: Judge
judge.body: The model looks at both photographs and a close crop of each area. It answers no change, wear or damage, and says how sure it is.

price.title: Price
price.body: Each finding is matched to the shop's published list. An amount is never the model's output.

decide.title: Decide
decide.body: A named person accepts, reduces, removes or adds. Only then can anything be charged.

findings.title: Every difference gets a plain answer.
findings.lead: Each one comes with its confidence, in words a renter can read.
findings.caption: Example findings. Illustrative photographs.

damage.title: Scratched frame
damage.body: Not there at handover. Matched to the price list and sent to a person.

wear.title: Light tyre wear
wear.body: Covered by the shop's wear policy. Never charged.

same.title: Down tube scuff
same.body: Already there at handover. It stays on the item's record and is never charged.

unsure.title: Glare on the brake
unsure.body: The photograph does not allow an answer. A person looks at the item itself.

accuracy.title: Measured, not claimed.
accuracy.lead: The comparison is tested on pairs of photographs whose true answer is known: clean returns, ordinary wear and real damage, in good light and bad.

counts.title: Published as counts
counts.body: Each result is a number of pairs out of the pairs tested, never a bare percentage.

renter.title: The renter's number comes first
renter.body: How often a clean return was wrongly flagged is the headline figure.

worse.title: It cannot quietly get worse
worse.body: A new version that does worse on the test is not released.

status.title: The scorecard is not published yet.
status.body: It appears here, with every count, once the evaluation set has been run.

agents.title: An agent acts only inside limits a person wrote.
agents.lead: A renter or an owner may let an AI agent act for them. Every tool call passes one gateway. It checks who is asking, for which shop and under which written limit, then records the call.
agents.caption: What an agent's tools may do

read.name: Read
read.body: Returns records the person may see.

draft.name: Draft

propose.name: Propose
propose.body: Prepares a decision for a person to approve.

notify.name: Notify
notify.body: Sends a fixed message, such as a reminder that a return is due.

mandate.name: Act under a mandate
mandate.body: Acts inside limits a person wrote in advance, and can be stopped at any time.

charge.name: Charge
charge.body: There is no such tier. No tool takes an amount, and no agent can start a charge.

advantages.title: Why a PayPal hold, not a card hold.
advantages.lead: Three differences matter to a rental shop.

days.title: It lasts as long as real rentals do
days.body: A PayPal hold can stay open for up to 29 days. Many card holds expire in about a week.

wallet.title: No card handed over
wallet.body: A renter paying from a PayPal wallet does not give a card to a shop they have never visited.

truth.title: PayPal's record is the truth
truth.body: A hold counts as placed, taken or released only after PayPal confirms it. Hold never guesses a payment's status.

lifecycle.title: The life of one hold.
lifecycle.lead: Four calls to PayPal. Hold records each step only after PayPal confirms it.

order.title: The deposit becomes its own order
order.body: It is separate from the rental fee, and it is created to reserve, not to charge.

authorize.title: The renter approves, and the hold is placed
authorize.body: {amount} is reserved in the renter's own account. No payment has happened.

renew.title: A late charge is still assured
renew.body: If a charge comes after the first three days, Hold renews the hold just before it. PayPal gives it a new identifier, and Hold follows it.

capture.title: Only the approved claim is taken
capture.body: {taken} is taken as the final capture. PayPal releases the other {released}.

void.title: The whole hold is released
void.body: All {amount} is freed at the counter. No payment ever happened.

lifecycle.idempotency: Every call that moves money carries its own request identifier, so a retry never takes it twice.

priceList.title: Damage price list
priceList.wear: Ordinary wear, such as light tyre wear or small scuffs on the pedals, is never charged.
priceList.agreed: Agreed by the renter before the hold is approved.

charge.a: No. A hold reserves the amount in the renter's own PayPal account. Nothing is taken unless a person approves a claim.

length.q: How long can a hold stay open?
length.a: Up to 29 days. Hold keeps it valid during the rental and flags any hold that is close to its end before it lapses.

beyond.q: What if the damage costs more than the hold?
beyond.a: The hold is taken in full and the balance is billed separately, with the same photographs attached.

app.q: Does anyone need an app or an account?
app.a: No. Staff open Hold in the browser on the phone they already carry. The renter gets a link.

dark.q: What if a photograph is too dark to judge?
dark.a: Hold asks for it again while the item is still at the counter. If it still cannot tell, it says so and a person looks at the item itself.

wear.q: Who decides what counts as ordinary wear?
wear.a: The shop does, once, in plain words. Hold applies that policy the same way to every renter.

release.a: The moment staff confirm a clean return, usually while you are still at the counter. Your phone tells you that nothing was charged.

chargedFor.q: What can I be charged for?
chargedFor.a: Only damage that is on the published price list, shown in the photographs and approved by a person. A claim can never be higher than the list.

disagree.q: What if I disagree with a claim?
disagree.a: You say so on the same screen and can add your own photographs. A named person at the shop looks at both sides and can lower or drop the charge.

photographs.a: They show the item, not you. Faces are blurred, and records are kept only as long as the shop's policy and the law require.

problems.no_passkey: There is no passkey for this address yet. Sign in with the emailed code, then add one.
problems.invitation_closed: This invitation can no longer be used.
problems.confirm_first: Adding another passkey needs one you already have. Confirm with it first.

invite.title: Join {shop} on Hold.
invite.lead: You are invited as {role}. Hold will email a code to {email} to confirm it is you.

aside.title: What working with Hold looks like.
aside.lead: Photographs at handover and at return, a hold in the renter's own PayPal account, and a person approving every charge.

closed.title: This invitation cannot be used.
closed.lead: Invitations work once, for seven days.
closed.body: Ask the shop's owner to send you a new one.
closed.missing: There is no invitation at this address.

noShop.title: No shop yet.
noShop.body: This account has no shop. Create one on the sign-up page with the same email, or ask a shop's owner to invite you.

passkey.title: Add a passkey
passkey.body: Your fingerprint, face or PIN on this device. Hold asks for it before anyone changes prices, staff or PayPal.

prices.title: Write your price list
prices.body: What each kind of damage costs, in plain words. Renters read it before they rent.

paypal.title: Connect your shop's PayPal account
paypal.body: Holds stay in your renters' own accounts, and approved claims are paid into yours.

staff.title: Invite your staff
staff.body: Each person signs in with their own email, with the role and approval limit you give them.

passkeyGate.title: Confirm it is you.
passkeyGate.confirmBody: Changing prices, staff or PayPal needs your passkey, not only an emailed code.
passkeyGate.addBody: Changing prices, staff or PayPal needs a passkey. Add one on this device first.

results.signed_out: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
results.role: Your role in this shop does not allow this.
results.invalid: Something in the form is missing or too long. Check it and try again.
results.unavailable: That did not work. Try again in a moment.
results.role_not_invitable: You cannot invite someone with that role.
results.currency_unset: Publish your price list first, so approval limits have a currency.
results.limit_invalid: The approval limit is not an amount. Use digits, such as 150 or 150.00.
results.email_failed: The invitation email could not be sent, so nothing was kept. Check the address and try again.
results.not_open: That invitation is no longer open.
results.currency_unknown: Choose a currency from the list.
results.rows_mismatched: Every price needs a description, a kind and an amount.
results.amount_invalid: Price {row} is not an amount. Use digits, such as 35 or 35.50.
results.threshold_invalid: The approval threshold is not an amount. Use digits, such as 200 or 200.00.
results.too_many_entries: A price list can have up to 60 prices.
results.description_too_long: The description of price {row} is too long.
results.description_repeated: Price {row} repeats another description. Make each one different.
results.amount_zero: Price {row} is zero. Remove it, or give it an amount.
results.wear_policy_missing: Say what counts as ordinary wear.
results.wear_policy_too_long: The wear policy is too long.
results.currency_fixed: The currency is fixed once a price list is published.
results.paypal_refused: PayPal did not accept these credentials. Check that you copied both from the same sandbox app.
results.paypal_unavailable: PayPal could not be reached. Nothing was kept. Try again in a moment.

security.title: Security
security.lead: A passkey signs you in with your fingerprint, face or PIN, on a device you hold.
security.leadRequired: Your role lets you change prices, staff or PayPal, so Hold asks for a passkey before you do: your fingerprint, face or PIN on a device you hold. An emailed code alone is not enough.
security.unavailable: Your passkeys could not be listed just now.
security.how: Your device keeps the passkey. Hold and its sign-in service keep only the public half, which cannot sign you in on its own.
security.confirmToAdd: Adding another passkey needs one you already have, so nobody who reaches your inbox can add their own.

invite.title: Invite someone
invite.lead: They receive an email with a link. It works once, for seven days, and only for the address you enter.
invite.limit: Largest claim they may approve, in {currency}
invite.limitNeedsCurrency: Counter staff can approve claims once your price list sets the shop's currency. Until then they approve nothing.

prices.title: Prices
prices.none: No price list is published yet. Renters see it before they rent, and every claim is priced from it.
prices.current: Version {version} is published, since {date}. Publishing again makes a new version. Rentals already booked keep the version their renter agreed to.
prices.readOnly: Only the owner or a manager can publish prices.
prices.threshold: Claims above this go to the owner or a manager, in {currency}
prices.thresholdHelp: Optional. Leave it empty and each staff member's own limit decides.
prices.wearHelp: Renters are never charged for this. Say it in plain words.
prices.publishHelp: The currency is fixed once the first price list is published.

paypal.title: PayPal
paypal.lead: Holds are placed in your renters' own PayPal accounts, and approved claims are paid into your shop's. Hold never keeps the money.

steps.app: At developer.paypal.com, open Apps & Credentials, choose Sandbox, and open the app of your shop's sandbox business account.
steps.copy: Copy its client ID and its secret.
steps.paste: Paste both below. Hold checks them with PayPal before keeping them.

paypal.sandboxOnly: This build connects sandbox accounts only. The credentials are kept in AWS Secrets Manager and are never shown again.
paypal.ownerOnly: Only the shop's owner can connect PayPal.

invitation.subject: You are invited to {shop} on Hold
invitation.body:
{inviter} invites you to work at {shop} on Hold, as {role}.

Open this link to accept. It works once, for seven days:
{link}

Hold will email you a code to confirm the address is yours. If you did not expect this, you can ignore it.
